body.statement: For every \(v\in\Delta(\mathcal B)\) and every \(0\le\gamma\le\Gamma_{\mathrm{vac}}\), summation by parts gives \(\sum_bd_b(v)m_b=-\sum_{j=1}^{B-1}D_j(v)(m_{j+1}-m_j)\). Consequently, \(\mathsf B_\gamma(v)\) equals the value of the finite linear program over increments \(\delta_j=m_{j+1}-m_j\) with \(\sum_j|\delta_j|\le\gamma\) and \(-M\le c+\sum_{k<b}\delta_k\le M\); an endpoint optimizer yields an extremal fixed control schedule. In particular, \(\mathsf B_\gamma(v)=\gamma\max_{j<B}|D_j(v)|\) when \(0\le\gamma\le2M\), and \(\mathsf B_{\Gamma_{\mathrm{vac}}}(v)=M\sum_b|d_b(v)|\).
body.justification: The cumulative-discrepancy map turns calendar robustness into an exact finite bias penalty for every sensitivity budget.
body.gap: ArmstrongKolesar2018 optimizes worst-case bias over convex regression classes, while BofillRoigEtAl2022 reports model-dependent trend bias; neither gives this ordered-block finite-population support function.
body.consumer: ACTT analysts can translate a clinically chosen drift budget into an exact bias allowance for any NCC weight vector.
